declarations.doc: `.dot`: the live marker, a 10dp accent dot that breathes. [delayMs] staggers a row of them (typing dots start 150ms apart).
`.cap` with `.ind`: a white pill of equal segments, the selected one marked by a sliding paper pill.
`.cb`: a 22dp rounded box, white with a grey edge, filled accent with a white tick once on.
`.cta`: the 52dp pill that carries a screen's one main action.
`.fl`: a 44dp circle that floats on the page with its own shadow; [flat] drops the fill and shadow, for the small actions inside a row.
declarations.source:
@Composable
fun FloatButton(
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    label: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    size: Dp = 44.dp,
    enabled: Boolean = true,
    flat: Boolean = false,
    container: Color = LocalPullsColors.current.raised,
    /** The one main action on a screen (Send) sounds at full weight; the rest are quiet. */
    emphasis: Emphasis = Emphasis.Subtle,
    content: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit,
) {
    Box(
        modifier
            .size(size)
            .then(if (flat) Modifier else Modifier.floatShadow(CircleShape))
            .clip(CircleShape)
            .background(if (flat) Color.Transparent else container)
            .semantics { contentDescription = label }
            .cueClickable(emphasis = emphasis, enabled = enabled, role = Role.Button, onClickLabel = label, onClick = onClick)
            .alpha(if (enabled) 1f else 0.4f),
        contentAlignment = Alignment.Center,
        content = content,
    )
}

declarations.doc: A [FloatButton] holding one prototype icon.

A page's bar in the one pill: [content] is what sits in it, after a search glass when [search], with the pill's end
made for a round button when [button]. [trailing] sits beside the pill, as the Inbox's sort does, and leaves with the
page. With [compact] the pill is short and reads that one word, centred, until a tap ([onExpand]) opens it to the full
width with its field focused ("a shorter bar that says Ask. And when you tap on it ... it kind of expands", Q5).
[veil] dims or holds the bar with its page. Outside a [FootBarLayer] the bar draws here, placed by [modifier].
`.okd`: a 14dp green dot with a white tick, for a finished step.

`.orb`: the live mark for AI work. While it works, a comet ring turns round a breathing dot. When
[done] turns true the ring finishes the turn it is on and then settles into a still wash with a
tick (rule 72); one that starts out done is already still. [idle] is the same still wash with a small
dot instead of the tick, for work that has not run, or did not finish, so a tick never claims
something that was not done. [stop] turns the breathing dot into a small square, because the orb is
then the Stop button (rule 87). No robot, compass or sparkle: those marks were dropped (rule 48).
`.pend`: a hollow 10dp ring for a step that has not started.
`.pill`: the quiet 44dp action beside the one main one (Retry, Stop, Rewrite): paper fill, medium 15sp ink, no shadow.

`.ask`: the raised pill that holds a one-line question or comment at the bottom of a page, its action inside at the
right. It is the kit's one field in its page frame, so it has Home's search pill's height, padding and words (rule
132; N6).
The avatar placeholder: the prototype's warm gradient disc.
The tour ring: a grey track and an accent arc for [n] of [of] stops, moving to a new count over 400ms.
The tour ring filled to [fraction] (0 to 1) as given, for a ring that follows the tour's scroll without jumps (rule 97).
`.r-qa button`: a 72dp tile with an icon over a label.

The list a sheet picks from, with a [SheetSearch] over it once it is longer than [searchFrom] rows: themes, models,
past chats. Most sheets are easier with a search ("most bottom sheets that we have actually benefit a lot from
search": recording 15 Oct 15:37, 12:28 to 12:36; L4, L23, L36), so every picking list is this one component. [group]
splits the rows under small headings in their order, each run in its own card; [row] draws one, told whether it is
the first in its card. [text] is what a search matches, every word in any order (rule 101).

`.sheet`: a paper sheet with 24dp top corners, a grabber, and a header of round close button, centered
title and a spacer, or the round [trailing] button in its place (Ask's new chat). The body scrolls
under the header, which stays put. Every sheet rests at two heights and slides between them (rule 77):
its normal height, which is its content up to half the screen, and its tall height near the top of the
screen, which a short sheet reaches too: the room under its content is the sheet's own paper. [full]
makes the body fill the sheet (chat, Commands); its normal height is then half the screen, and its
[footer] stays on screen at either height, floating over the body, which runs on under it and dissolves into the
paper as the Tour's page does under its Ask bar ([aboveFooter] floats just over the footer, as Ask's
scroll-to-the-end button). [expandable] off keeps a sheet at its normal height. [back] swaps the close X for a back
arrow. [tall] opens it at its tall height (Commands, whose search takes the keyboard; Ask).

The sheet is the kit's own window, not Material's. It rises from below the screen on a spring with a little bounce
while fading in through a 2px blur, and leaves in 350ms on the smooth-out curve (rule 73, H3). It follows a finger:
dragged up from its normal height it goes to the tall one, down from the tall height to the normal one, and down
from the normal height it closes, settling on the same spring at the speed it was let go. Only a drag that starts
with the content at its top moves the sheet: scrolling the content back up to its top, or a fling that runs into
it, never takes the sheet down with it (H2). A sheet is always a bottom sheet, wherever it was opened from (H6).
A field that takes the keyboard lifts it to the tall height, so the field never sits behind the keyboard.

declarations.source:
@Composable
fun PullsSheet(
    onClose: () -> Unit,
    title: String,
    full: Boolean = false,
    back: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    footer: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    scroll: ScrollState? = null,
    expandable: Boolean = true,
    trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    tall: Boolean = false,
    aboveFooter: (@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit)? = null,
    content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit,
) = PullsSheet(onClose, { SheetTitle(title) }, full, back, footer, scroll, expandable, trailing, tall, aboveFooter, content)

/**
 * A sheet whose pages slide inside it (rule 78). Language from Settings, Select model from the Analyze
 * card, Effort from the model list: the panel, the lip and the header stay where they are, the ✕ turns
 * into ← and the body slides sideways through a 3px blur, a third of the sheet's width over 350ms, far and slow
 * enough to see which way it went: forward from the right, ← to the right (H1). [parent]
 * names the page ← goes back to (null for the first page); [onPage] changes the page, so the caller
 * owns where it is. Each page keeps its own scroll position, so back finds a list where it was left.
 * At its normal height the panel grows or shrinks to the next page's height as the body slides. [heading] draws a
 * page's title itself where plain text is not enough (the pull request's name and number); [title] is still its name.
 */

declarations.doc:
A sheet whose pages slide inside it (rule 78). Language from Settings, Select model from the Analyze
card, Effort from the model list: the panel, the lip and the header stay where they are, the ✕ turns
into ← and the body slides sideways through a 3px blur, a third of the sheet's width over 350ms, far and slow
enough to see which way it went: forward from the right, ← to the right (H1). [parent]
names the page ← goes back to (null for the first page); [onPage] changes the page, so the caller
owns where it is. Each page keeps its own scroll position, so back finds a list where it was left.
At its normal height the panel grows or shrinks to the next page's height as the body slides. [heading] draws a
page's title itself where plain text is not enough (the pull request's name and number); [title] is still its name.
`.r-card`: a white 16dp card on the sheet's paper, [gap] below what comes before it.

A field inside a sheet's white card: the label small and muted over the text, a hairline above it
unless it is the [first] row. [minLines] above one makes it a note area; [trailing] is for a word
such as Show, never an icon.

A heading over a card on a sheet, the one kind every sheet uses: the Settings sheet's small muted words and nothing
else, no count, no chevron and no line under it, and it folds nothing ("we get rid of this number, we get rid of this
divider, we get rid of this chevron, we keep them consistent": recording 16 Oct 09:50, 02:55 to 04:05; M7). [extra]
sits at its end, for the + and − a group of files shows (L20). [first] is the heading right under the ✕ or a search.

`.r-mrow`: a 52dp row, a 22dp icon column, the label, and a trailing value; a hairline above it
starts after the icon column. [first] drops that hairline. [detail] is a second, muted line under the label.

`.find`: the search field at the top of a sheet's list (Repositories, Files, Commands). It is the kit's one field in its
sheet frame, made like the cards under it, white with their 16dp corners and their soft shadow, so it reads as part of
the list and not as a pill floating over it: the magnifier, the placeholder in the muted ink, and ✕ to clear once
something is typed. The keyboard's [imeAction] runs [onAction], or puts the keyboard away when there is none.

`.sk`: a 12dp bar standing in for content that is still arriving. A soft light band, 40% of the bar wide, sweeps across it
from left to right every 1200ms on a linear curve (rule 85). With the system setting "Remove animations" it sits still.
A list's first rows: a number, a title and a meta line, laid out like the Inbox rows they stand in for.
`.chip`: a 36dp outlined pill; selected it fills with `--chipOn`. [count] is muted and tabular.
`.tog`: a 52x32 switch.

`.toast`: a dark pill above the bottom bars; it leaves after 2.4s, or 4.2s when it offers an action.
It rises 16dp from 97% size through a 2px blur in 350ms and leaves in 250ms (the Toast recipe, rule 73).

`.tb`: text tabs on a hairline, the selected one underlined in the accent. Each tab is a 48dp-tall target that reaches
halfway to its neighbours, so the space between two labels hits one of them; the underline stays as wide as the label.
[spread] lays the labels across the whole width, the first at the start and the last at the end with even gaps
between. When they do not fit with 16dp between them the labels step down to body size (15sp), and only when they
still do not fit does the row keep a 24dp gap and scroll sideways; a label is never cut.

The underline is one stroke that slides from tab to tab when the selection changes (250ms smooth-out), and leans
toward a neighbour by [pull] (-1 to 1, toward the next tab when positive) while a finger drags the page under it, so
it moves the way the page does (rule 105).
